name: Question 1
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y({x}^{2}+1),\,y(-1)=1
$$

Use the modified Euler method with one step to approximate $y(-\frac{1}{2}).$

$y(-\frac{1}{2})≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the modified Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=-\frac{1}{2},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=-\frac{1}{2}-(-1)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we add the initial condition data to a table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $1$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now, we compute the value of ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y({x}^{2}+1) \\  & =1((-1)^{2}+1) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ |  |  |  |  |

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ |  |  |  |

The coordinates of the initially predicted new point given by the predictor equation are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=-1+\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=1+1=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add the second value to the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ |  |  |

So, the predicted slope at this point is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={y}_{p}\cdot (({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1) \\  & =2\cdot ({(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+1) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ | $\frac{5}{2}$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+\frac{5}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ | $\frac{5}{2}$ | $\frac{9}{8}$ |

The value of $x$ in the next row is ${x}_{\text{new}}=2.$ To get the value of $y$ in the next row, we add $Δy$ to $y:$

$$
{y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy=1+\frac{9}{8}=\frac{17}{8}.
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ | $\frac{5}{2}$ | $\frac{9}{8}$ |
| $-\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{17}{8}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(-\frac{1}{2})≈\frac{17}{8}.$

Question 1

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=y(x2+1),y(−1)=1 Use the modified Euler method with one step to approximate y(−12).
y(−12)≈
178​
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y0=y(x0), the modified Euler method with step size Δx is given by Predictor:Δyp=y′⋅Δx,Corrector:Δy=12(y′+yp′)⋅Δx, where yp′=f(xnew,yp) is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point (xnew,yp)=(x+Δx,y+Δyp).

Since we want to find the value of y at x=−12, we will use a step size of Δx=−12−(−1)=12.

First, we add the initial condition data to a table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
−1 1

Now, we compute the value of y′ according to the given rule:

y′=y(x2+1)=1((−1)2+1)=2

So, we add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
−1 1 2

Next, we compute Δyp using the predictor equation:

Δyp=y′⋅Δx=2⋅12=1

We add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
−1 1 2 1

The coordinates of the initially predicted new point given by the predictor equation are

xnew=x+Δx=−1+12=−12,yp=y+Δyp=1+1=2.

Let's add the second value to the table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
−1 1 2 1 2

So, the predicted slope at this point is yp′=yp⋅((xnew)2+1)=2⋅((−12)2+1)=52.

We can add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
−1 1 2 1 2 52

Finally, we compute Δy using the corrector equation:

Δy=12(y′+yp′)⋅Δx=12(2+52)⋅12=14⋅92=98

We add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
−1 1 2 1 2 52 98

The value of x in the next row is xnew=2. To get the value of y in the next row, we add Δy to y: ynew=y+Δy=1+98=178.

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
−1 1 2 1 2 52 98
−12 178

Therefore, we conclude that y(−12)≈178.
